title: Occupant satisfaction in LEED and non-LEED certified buildings

stimuli.description: Actual commercial office buildings, either LEED certified (65 buildings) or non-LEED rated (79 buildings), with comparable age and size.

tables.description: Categories included in the CBE Occupant Indoor Environmental Quality Survey, listing IEQ parameters and general building/workspace satisfaction.
Description of the dataset used for the analysis, including number of buildings and occupant responses for LEED and non-LEED groups.
Summary statistics for year of construction/renovation and building size for LEED and non-LEED groups.
Distribution of occupants' responses in the dataset and comparison with all LEED certified commercial offices by LEED Rating and Version.

Distribution of occupants' responses in LEED and non-LEED buildings based on 'non-environmental' factors (spatial layout, distance from window, building size, gender, age, type of work, time at workspace, weekly working hours).

Mean and standard deviation values for LEED and non-LEED buildings, difference in means (ΔM), statistical significance (p-value), and effect size (Spearman Rho) for occupant satisfaction with building, workspace, and 15 IEQ parameters.

limitations: The collection of users' responses is not linked with direct appraisal and/or measurement of physical characteristics and IEQ parameters of the building and the workspace.
No systematic randomized approach has been enforced for building selection, so the dataset cannot be considered a representative sample of the building stock.

Other parameters not included in the CBE survey (e.g., the availability of a view out and the layers included in such view, location of the building) may have a significant influence on occupant satisfaction.
The greatest majority of the responses were obtained from buildings situated in the US (83%), so results mainly refer to the North American context.
The sample of buildings included in our analysis is only partially representative of the total amount of buildings rated by LEED to date, due to the continuous evolution of the LEED program.
The study did not consider the potential influence of the variation of 'non-environmental' factors on occupant satisfaction in LEED and non-LEED certified buildings.

Future studies need to investigate the possible correlation existing between satisfaction of occupants, LEED certification level (platinum, gold, silver, certified), LEED product, and their different versions.

An investigation of the individual scorecards of the buildings featured in the chosen dataset of the CBE survey database is necessary to ascertain the credit distribution under the IEQ category that each building has achieved, and correlate this with the votes of satisfaction.
